critical_code_review_comments: public_commerce.py — Signature verification is enforced only when STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET is set (line 156-157: fail-closed ONLY under sk_live). Preview .env has it empty so the /api/public/webhook endpoint currently accepts UNSIGNED POSTs — this is fine for TEST but the deploy checklist MUST populate STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET before enabling live keys. Idempotency (processed_webhook_events keyed by event_id) and the {payment_status:{$ne:'paid'}} guard prevent unauthorized fulfillment resets even in this state — verified live this iteration.

public_commerce.py:_grant_fulfillment — Correctly resets download_count to 0 ONLY on the pending→paid transition. A duplicate/replayed webhook or a poll after payment CANNOT re-open the 5-download budget. Confirmed live: downloaded once (count=1), replayed webhook, count remained 1.

QRUPurchaseSuccess.js — Polls /checkout/status/{sid} every 2s up to 12 attempts (~24s). In this run the paid state resolved in <4s (Stripe redirect already fired _grant_fulfillment via the status poll on first hit). Consider adding a 'Check again' manual retry button for the rare case where Stripe's confirmation is >24s, not blocking.

public_commerce.py:_epub_url — Falls back to book.artifacts.design.ebook.epub. Path is derived server-side, never leaked to client (verified: /api/public/books/{id} contains no 'epub'/'artifacts' markers). Consider adding a Pydantic PublicBookOut whitelist so a future accidental shallow-copy in a public serializer cannot regress this.
public_commerce.py — /webhook always returns 200 on our own logic errors so Stripe won't retry indefinitely; signature failure and malformed body return 400 (Stripe will retry per its policy). GOOD.
Louisiana governing-law clause is consistent with Ascend Development Group LLC ownership in the footer and matches the founder's declared jurisdiction. No mixed-jurisdiction language found.
